messages.subject: CIM
messages.body_plain:
Following up an earlier post...

If I understand correctly, this isn't quite like CIM because there is no "window" blocking the covariates when the covariate portion of the genome is being scanned.  i.e. some care will need to be taken to only analyze regions that don't contain covariates.

(Or am I missing something?)

Julin

messages.subject: R/qtl version 1.02-26
messages.body_plain:
A new version of R/qtl (1.02-26) has been released at its web site
(http://www.biostat.jhsph.edu/~kbroman/qtl).

See http://www.biostat.jhsph.edu/~kbroman/qtl/STATUS.txt for a list of
changes.  The major changes are the following:

  Modified scanone() and scantwo() so that they may analyze multiple
  phenotypes simultaneously.  This can greatly speed up the analyses
  with Haley-Knott regression (method="hk") and imputation
  (method="imp").  We can use this trick to speed up permutation
  tests: create multiple permuted phenotypes and then analyze them all
  at once.

  scanone() results no longer include parameter estimates (such as the
  phenotypic averages for each genotype group and the residual SD).
  The bookkeeping for this became too painful as we moved to allow
  multiple phenotypes to be analyzed simultaneously.  To get such
  estimates, use fitqtl().  fitqtl() currently works only via the
  imputation method, but we expect to soon implement multiple interval
  mapping (MIM) and also Haley-Knott regression.

  scantwo() with method="em" now works for the X chromosome, including
  with model="binary".

  Modified the "map10" dataset: a genetic map modeled after the mouse,
  with markers having an approximately 10 cM spacing.  We've revised
  the chromosome lengths to match those in the Mouse Genome Database.

  Dropped support for intercrosses with sex-specific maps (class
  "f2ss").

  Changed the meaning of the argument "lodcolumn" in scanone(). It now
  should be an index starting at 1 rather than 3.  I think this will
  be more clear for the case of LOD scores from multiple phenotypes,
  though perhaps it will be less clear.

  summary.scanone() now takes an argument "lodcolumn"; if a single
  scanone output is given as input, it picks off peaks using those LOD
  scores.  (As with plot.scanone, this is indexed starting at 1.)

  Similarly, added a "lodcolumn" argument to plot.scantwo() and
  summary.scantwo(), for the case that the scantwo results are for
  multiple phenotypes; only results for a single phenotype are used by
  these functions, and "lodcolumn" indicates which one.

As always, I'd appreciate hearing any suggestions or comments or
complaints.

Karl Broman

messages.body_plain:
Right.

I don't really like the windowing thing, but if you want to do that,
you'd need to run scanone
with all marker covariates and then with each omitted, one at a
time.  Then you'd need to paste
the results within a window around a covariate for the case it was
omitted back into the other
output.

karl

messages.subject: inbred outbred cross
messages.body_plain:
I want to ask if R/qtl is suitable for analysing inbred outbred cross
F2? or it only supports F2 from two inbred strains?

Thanks,
Paul

messages.subject: Re: inbred outbred cross
messages.body_plain:
Dear Paul,

I'm not entirely sure what you mean by an inbred outbred cross, but
if you have large sibships from outbred individuals, it should be
possible to do the analysis in R/qtl, though it won't be easy.

We have facilities to do the analysis of what I call a "phase-known
four-way cross", which is basically two parents with a lot of sibs.
The hard parts are getting the data into an appropriate form, and if
you have multiple large sibships, doing a combined analysis.

regards,
karl
